title: Grateful Dead Live at Carter-Finley Stadium on 1990-07-10
source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; 2 Nakamichi CM100/CP4 Shotguns + 1 Sennheiser 421 > Unknown Mixer (Either A Radio Shack Or Boss) 1/4 Inch In/RCA Out > Sony TC-D5m, Tapes:Maxell MX 90 + 100; Transfer With Nakamichi MR-1 > Korg MR-1000 @ 1 Bit/5.6 MHz; Tracking/Sample Rate Conversion With AudioGate Software To 32/96 kHz Wave; Dithered/Flacked With Korg Aqua To 16/44; SBE's Checked/Fixed With Trader's Little Helper; Metadata Tagging With Tag&Rename

ai_review.summary: A quirky North Carolina summer show marked by a hovering helicopter and rain‑induced power glitches; recording is listenable but shows occasional dropouts.
ai_review.review: Reviewers love the oddball circumstances of this concert – a helicopter circling the shade and a sudden downpour that caused a power glitch – making it a memorable experience they wouldn’t trade. The audio suffers from brief glitches tied to the power issue, but overall fans consider it worth listening despite the technical hiccups.

ai_rating.rationale: Only one five‑star review; strong enthusiasm for the show's uniqueness outweighs lack of concrete recording details, leading to a solid but cautious rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Power glitch during rain caused occasional audio dropouts; no specific comments on soundboard vs. audience source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Unusual, weather‑affected performance with a memorable helicopter incident; overall vibe is quirky and enjoyable despite technical interruptions.
